WhatsApp evidence primarily supports the commitment and social aspects.

mainEntity.name: Are WhatsApp messages admissible as evidence in civil court?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes. WhatsApp messages are widely admissible as electronic documentary evidence in civil courts (under UK CPR Part 32/33, US Federal Rules of Evidence Rule 901/902, and similar Commonwealth statutes), provided their authenticity and provenance can be established with clear timestamps, sender identification, and an intact chain of custody.

mainEntity.name: What is Bates numbering and why is it mandatory for court bundles?

acceptedAnswer.text: Bates numbering is a sequential page-identification system (e.g., EXHIBIT-0001, EXHIBIT-0002) used by judges, solicitors, and barristers to cite specific pages during hearings and cross-examinations. Unpaginated screenshot piles are frequently rejected by court clerks.

mainEntity.name: How does SHA-256 cryptographic hashing prove chat integrity?

acceptedAnswer.text: A cryptographic SHA-256 hash creates a unique 64-character digital fingerprint of the original raw WhatsApp export file. If even a single comma or emoji is altered, the hash changes completely. ChatDocket computes this hash locally using the browser Web Crypto API and stamps it onto every page.

mainEntity.name: Can I redact sensitive personal information before filing in court?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes. Court rules require redaction of non-material personal data like credit card numbers, national insurance/SSN numbers, and home addresses. ChatDocket provides 1-click bulk PII redaction and interactive black-out bars that preserve surrounding context without wiping out the entire dialogue.
